newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge sets Interpol on IBM case fugitives.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge sets Interpol on IBM case fugitives.

text.p: A judge investigating a bribery scandal involving the Argentine unit of International Business Machines Corp said on Wednesday he had asked Interpol to issue an international arrest warrant for four men.

They are the former president of state bank Banco Nacion, Aldo Dadone; the former president and vice-president of IBM Argentina, Ricardo Matorana and Gustavo Soriani; and former Cabinet official Juan Carlos Cattaneo.
Argentine Federal Judge Adolfo Bagnasco told local radio: "They will have no alternative but to give themselves up. If we don't do this, we will be encouraging fugitives."

The deputy head of the Banco Nacion, Alfredo Aldaco, gave himself up last week after Bagnasco ordered the arrest and custody of the men pending trial. All have been sacked from their jobs because of the scandal.
The judge suspects bribes were paid in 1993 to ensure IBM won a $250 million contract to install a computer system for the national bank.
He said in his ruling: "The market price of products and services accepted by Banco Nacion was about 50 percent lower than that charged by IBM Argentina SA."
The former Nacion, IBM and government officials have been charged with bribery, while Dadone and Aldaco are also charged with embezzling public funds.
IBM has denied any wrongdoing, but has admitted to errors "inconsistent with company policy." Other IBM contracts in Argentina have been the subject of separate bribery probes.
